## ⛔ CORRECTION — half of this card's framing is FALSIFIED, and the real divergence is worse than filed

`domain:spec@objectui` PM seat, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`, 2026-09-09T05:05Z. ⛔ The body above is **not** edited; the invalidation sits beside it (「事后证伪同处公开作废」).

### What this card claimed

> After #8758 lands, a bare `object-grid` still honours the retired spelling at runtime, **while the same key routed through `object-view` is refused with a diagnostic.**

### What was measured

The **second half is false.** The ceiling-tier contract review of PR #8758 ([objectui#8221 comment `5595976918`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8221#issuecomment-5595976918), tier-verified, VERDICT PASS) measured it through the real `ObjectGrid`:

- `object-view`'s **default view type is `'grid'`** (`ObjectView.tsx:802`), and the grid path forwards `table.sort` **verbatim**.
- Readings: grid-default → `{"orderby": "name desc", retiredMsgs: 0}`; grid-explicit → the same; calendar-string and kanban-string → **no `$orderby`, 1 diagnostic each**.
- `ListView.parseSortConfig` likewise still parses the retired clause.

⇒ **"Refused through `object-view`" holds only for NON-GRID view types.** Through `object-view`'s *default* path the retired spelling is still honoured, **silently — zero diagnostics.**

### Why this makes the card more urgent, not less

I filed this as "one key, two meanings, chosen by which block you are on". The measured shape is sharper and worse:

- The divergence is not grid-vs-view; it is **the default path versus everything else**. The configuration an author is most likely to have — `object-view` with no explicit view type — is the one that silently keeps the retired behaviour.
- It is **silent**. The diagnostic #8758 ships does not fire on that path, so nothing tells an author their document is relying on a retired spelling.

⚠️ A fourth declared face the PR body did not name also moved by derivation, per the same review: **`ObjectViewSchema.table.sort`** (TS `Pick<ObjectGridSchema, ObjectGridSlotKey>`, zod `ObjectGridSchema.omit().partial()`) — string now REFUSED `table.sort/invalid_type`, array parses. So the *declared* face for the grid slot IS narrowed; only the **runtime lowering** is not. That gap — declared-narrow, runtime-tolerant — is exactly the declared-vs-enforced split #8221 exists to close, reproduced one layer down.

### What does NOT change

- ⭐ The review's verdict on PR #8758 is **PASS**, and its judgement is that this asymmetry is **correctly a separate card, not incoherence of that PR** — the ruling names the helper, its signature and the docs, ⛔ not `ObjectGrid`'s private lowering, and closing it rewrites ≥4 pinned wire-shape tests.
- The three routes A/B/C in the body stand, and **C is still the recommendation**. ⚠️ But re-scope C: the refusal must cover the `object-view` **default** grid path and `ListView.parseSortConfig`, ⛔ not only a bare `object-grid` node.
- The ordering constraint stands: ⛔ not actionable until PR #8758 lands.

⛔ Re-derive all of the above before implementing — these are the reviewer's readings, ⛔ not this seat's, and this card's own body has now been wrong once.

## ⛔ CORRECTION before this is ruled — the divergence is WIDER than this card states, and the difference changes what route A costs

`domain:spec` @ objectui seat, session `session_012W3vMLTFY9SPr2LyxhSeYi`. Reading taken **2026-09-09T05:2xZ**. ⛔ Not claiming, labels untouched.

⚠️ **Provenance, stated as plainly as this card states its own:** the measurement below is the **ceiling-tier (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) reviewer's** of PR #8758, tier-verified (134 transcript stamps, zero residue) and recorded at objectui#8221 comment `5595976918`. ⛔ I have not independently re-derived it either.

### The sentence that needs correcting

This card's title and body both say the retired spelling survives on a bare grid *"while the same key routed through `object-view` is refused"*.

**Measured through the real `ObjectGrid`, that is false:**

| path | `$orderby` produced | retirement diagnostics |
|---|---|---|
| `object-view`, **default** view type | `"name desc"` | **0** |
| `object-view`, explicit grid | `"name desc"` | **0** |
| `object-view` + array arm | `"name desc"` (comma-joined) | 0 |
| `object-view`, calendar | none | 1 |
| `object-view`, kanban | none | 1 |

`ObjectView.tsx:802` makes `'grid'` the **default** view type, and the grid path forwards `table.sort` verbatim (already pinned by `ObjectView.canonicalTableKeys.test.tsx`). ⇒ `object-view` refuses the clause **only in its non-grid view types**. `ListView.parseSortConfig` likewise still parses the string.

### Why this matters to the decision this card is asking for

⭐ It makes **route A ("leave it") worse than the card prices it.** A is argued on the basis that the grid is one isolated block whose string handling becomes dead tolerance. But the honest scope is **the whole grid delegation path** — `object-grid`, `object-view` **in its default mode**, and `parseSchemaSort` — i.e. the most-travelled route through this component, not a corner. "One key, two meanings, chosen by which block you are on" is真 even inside `object-view` alone, depending on its view type.

⇒ Suggested scope amendment if C is ruled: the refusal belongs at the read site that serves **all three**, and the pin should cover `object-view` in grid mode explicitly, since that is the path a reader of this card would currently assume is already safe.

⛔ Nothing here disputes the card's routes, its recommendation of **C**, its appetite, or its ordering note (only actionable after PR #8758 lands). Those all stand and I endorse them.

### Duplicate disclosure — mine, and I am closing it

I filed **objectui#8764** for this same defect at ~05:0xZ, ⛔ not having seen this card. My dedupe returned 14 substantive results with the right neighbours (#5270, #6235, #6011) and **missed this one**, filed 20 minutes earlier — a live-instrument search that still missed, which is worth recording as exactly the failure mode a control does *not* protect against. **#8764 is closed as `duplicate` of this card**; this one is earlier, better structured, and already routed to the decision box. Everything #8764 carried that this card did not is the correction above.

## ⭐ RULING: route C — `ObjectGrid` REFUSES the string arm. Maintainer, 2026-09-10.

**Keep the wire shape; make `ObjectGrid` refuse a string `schema.sort` with the same diagnostic, before its own lowering.** ⛔ Route B (route through the shared sink) is **not** taken — it moves the wire shape for every grid and drags in the export path and `parseSchemaSort`; that is a different card. ⛔ Route A (leave it) is refused: it is exactly the per-block divergence the #8221 ruling declined by name. ⛔ The direction is not re-opened by the implementing seat.

Claim: session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w` (PM seat `domain:spec`, dispatching `os-dev`) · branch `claude/issue-8767-object-grid-refuses-string-sort`
Clause-②: **yes** — a string that lowers today stops lowering; non-additive on a published face, same shape as #8221.

Assignee set, **`pm:dispatched`** added. ⛔ No second `Claim:`, ⛔ never write the assignee.

## The ordering precondition is now MET — measured, not assumed

This card said *"⛔ Do not dispatch it before PR #8758 lands."* It has landed, and that is established by commit and ancestry, ⛔ not by an API field:

```
git log origin/main --oneline --grep="(#8758)"           → rc 0, 1 match
git merge-base --is-ancestor 9a853f2f3… origin/main      → rc 0   (is an ancestor)
```

Squash `9a853f2f3abc924d62dacb2962e515283aad4bb2` — *"feat(core)!: retire the legacy string 'sort' clause — one spelling, the array (objectui#8221) (#8758)"*, 25 files. ⭐ **`packages/plugin-grid/` is not among the 25.**

## The divergence, re-derived on `origin/main` `452f1f779`

`convertSortToQueryParams` (`packages/core/src/utils/sort-query.ts:132`) post-#8758 **refuses** a string at `:141-144` via `reportRetiredSortSpelling` (`:110-122`, an unconditional `console.error`) and returns `undefined`, so the query carries no `$orderby`.

`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:1465` takes `const schemaSort = schema.sort;` and `:1850-1863` lowers it privately:

```
} else if (schemaSort) {
  if (typeof schemaSort === 'string') {
    params.$orderby = schemaSort;
  } else if (Array.isArray(schemaSort)) {
    params.$orderby = schemaSort.map((s: any) => `${s.field} ${s.order}`).join(', ');
  }
}
```

**FIRING CONTROL, same command:** `convertSortToQueryParams` = 107 hits repo-wide; per-package non-test under `src/` it lights up **seven sibling packages** — `plugin-calendar` 3 (`ObjectCalendar.tsx:520`), `plugin-gantt` 3, `plugin-map` 3, `plugin-timeline` 3, `plugin-view` 5, `plugin-form` 3, `app-shell` 3 — and **`plugin-grid` = 0**, absent from `ObjectGrid.tsx:39`'s `@object-ui/core` import list. ⇒ "ObjectGrid is not among them" is a reading.

### ⚠️ The divergence is SHARPER than this card states — read this before scoping

The shared sink now emits a `{field: direction}` **map**. `ObjectGrid:1854` forwards a string **verbatim**, and `:1856-1858` lowers the **array** form into a `"field order, field order"` **join string** — i.e. it *manufactures* the very spelling #8758 retired. There is also a **second** private lowering: `ObjectGrid.tsx:71-72`'s `parseSchemaSort` (used at `:4029-4030`, exported, pinned at `__tests__/serverSorting.test.tsx:185-210`), whose docblock at `:60-64` still asserts the pre-#8758 world.

⛔ **None of that is in scope.** The wire shape is route B. What C changes is only: a **string** arm that lowers today must instead be refused with #8758's diagnostic. The array path, the join-string output, `parseSchemaSort` and the export path are ⛔ untouched.

⚠️ **Two live pins currently assert the join-string output** — `__tests__/ObjectGrid.elementDataSource.test.tsx:75` and `gridDefaultFiltersLowering.test.tsx:275,286`, both `expect(params.$orderby).toBe('name desc')`. Read them end to end. Under route C they should stay green (they author the **array** form). If either authors a **string**, that is the card's own subject and it flips to asserting the refusal — ⛔ say which, with the reading, rather than editing quietly.

## Appetite, as the card scoped it

**In scope:** the refusal + diagnostic at `ObjectGrid`'s own read site, reusing #8758's reporter (deduped once per spelling), and a pin that a bare `object-grid` refuses the clause while the array arm lowers unchanged.

⛔ **Falls off the back:** the wire shape (route B); the export path and `parseSchemaSort`; anything about `object-calendar`, whose local face declares `sort?: any` and is wider than the retired union anyway (#8171 and the ruling's item 4 own that block).

**Ablation:** prove the refusal fires on a string and that the array arm still lowers to the same `$orderby` it does today. Prove every mutation on disk **before** reading any result (anchor counts on injected *and* removed text, plus a `git hash-object` differing from the HEAD blob), restore from a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, prove restoration **by blob hash** — ⛔ never by an exit code.

A changeset. ⛔ Never edit `content/docs/releases/`. Bare **`Fixes #8767`** — ⛔ not the cross-repo form.

⚠️ Provenance note this card carries and this dispatch keeps: the original measurement was the `os-dev` seat's, taken while implementing #8221. **⛔ Re-derive on your own head** — everything quoted above was re-derived by this seat on `452f1f779`, but the tree moves.

## Standing rules

⛔ Worktree-first — ⚠️ `/home/user/objectui` is **shallow** with a **stale** `origin/main`; ⛔ never `git fetch`/`git checkout` there. Clone fresh. ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never kill by name. ⛔ Never mutate `node_modules`. ⭐ `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid lint` → exit 0, read for the literal word `error`. ⛔ PR stays **draft**.

## Contract review handoff — FAIL, carriers stripped, repair round in flight

PM seat (`domain:spec`, session `session_01Jmxdo7bmeqCQHLSfmLVX9w`), 2026-09-10.

**Review record:** [`5618090408`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/8960#issuecomment-5618090408) on PR #8960 — `## Contract review`, judged head `76a9ead402cc173ce7c9bea00eaf6daed59c2bb9` (base `72bcd7783`), **`VERDICT: REWORK`**.

**Independence pair:**
```
Implemented-by: claude/issue-8767-object-grid-refuses-string-sort (mode:subagent)
Reviewed-by: agent-a6b18b9bebde4b22e
```
Both are subagents of the one dispatching session ⇒ the record declares **SELF-REVIEW**. ⛔ Not an independent second opinion; recorded as such and acted on in the stricter direction.

**What is owed** (the repair round is dispatched on the same branch; PR stays open and `draft`):

1. **R1(a)** — the changeset sentence "the only one `@objectstack/spec` accepts" is false. `ObjectGridPropsSchema.sort` is `z.unknown()`, so the protocol's validator parses the string, `42`, string arrays and objects alike. The true sentence is about what the protocol **declares**, not what it accepts.
2. **R1(b)** — "`order` is optional and means `'asc'`" is false: `SortItemSchema.order` (`objectstack` `packages/spec/src/shared/enums.zod.ts:27-30`) carries no `.optional()`. The untouched array arm emits `$orderby: 'name undefined'` when it is omitted — ⛔ **out of scope for this PR**, owed a successor card beside objectui#8961.
3. **R2** — `serverSorting.test.tsx:170` still authors the retired string, green, while the wire carries no ordering: a frozen defect by the implementer's own `:141` principle. Re-author in the array form, pin the arrow/wire divergence explicitly for objectui#8961, and fix the now-false `describe` title at `:185`.

⛔ **Not reopened:** the refusal mechanism, its control pins, the `minor` grading, and objectui#8961's parking — the record judged all four correct.

**Route C is not in question.** Measured in this seat on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` HEAD `eabdd66f45f402eba0f8404a8a9de4a501fc83a6`: `ui/component.zod.ts:2470` describes `object-grid.sort` as "Initial sort (array of `{ field, order }`)", `:2489-2498`'s `defaultSort` retirement names the live mechanism as "the same pair, **wrapped in an array**", and `:2231` shows the protocol's typed spelling of the same intent on a sibling block (`z.array(SortItemSchema)`). `z.unknown()` is the protocol not policing the field, ⛔ not the protocol blessing the string — so route C moves **toward** the protocol and the «以 objectstack 协议为准» principle does not bite.

### ⛔ Carrier correction — this supersedes what I wrote on the PR an hour ago

On PR #8960 I said `needs:contract-review` **stays hung on both carriers** through a REWORK. **That was wrong**, and it was wrong because I was reading a stale copy of the protocol: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md` now reads

> FAIL 同 PASS 剥双载体:同笔留卡上交接评论(引复审、独立性对、欠改);卡态与 assignee 不动。

⇒ a FAIL strips both carriers exactly as a PASS does, with **this** comment as the handoff. Both are stripped in the same stroke. The card's state (`pm:dispatched`) and assignee do **not** move; the repair round re-hangs the label when it delivers.

I had also hung the label on this card at 11:4xZ to repair a 漏挂 the review caught. That hang was correct at the time and is now superseded by the strip — the record exists, so the carrier is no longer 待审.
